findings.claim: The lesson makes an exhaustive technical claim that an assistant has exactly three inputs (standing instructions, shared context, and the current prompt), and the GIFT item at artifact.gift:7 marks chat history as not an input. Current coding assistants can also use conversation history and tool-managed memory/instruction layers, so this core model and its formative check are false as written.

evidence.section: Guide Copilot towards helpful outputs: GitHub tells users to delete an earlier request when it is no longer helpful context, or start a new conversation when none of a conversation's context is helpful.
CLAUDE.md vs auto memory and How CLAUDE.md files load: auto memory is loaded into every session, and multiple managed, user, project, local, and on-demand instruction files can enter context.

findings.recommendation: Keep the same syllabus objective but call these the three learner-controlled inputs in this lesson, not the assistant's only inputs. State that tools may also supply conversation history, system/organization instructions, memory, tool results, and automatically selected context. Update the objective, recap, HTML feedback, static alternative, and GIFT question/feedback so chat history is not taught as impossible.

findings.claim: The Share lane classifies any project code or documentation without secrets or personal data as safe to share. Confidential business information, proprietary algorithms, and source code can be sensitive even when they contain neither credentials nor personal data. The activity and GIFT quiz reinforce the same unsafe classification.

evidence.section: Sensitive Information Disclosure: sensitive information includes confidential business data and proprietary source code; consumers need to avoid unintentionally providing sensitive data, and access should follow least privilege.

findings.recommendation: Define Share as material explicitly permitted by the program/employer for that approved tool and account, with no secrets, personal data, confidential business data, proprietary code restrictions, or other sensitive content. Make the sample start.sh/README explicitly synthetic or authorized, and update the simulator, recap, static alternative, and GIFT feedback. Keep provider/plan retention caveats, but do not make approved-tool status the only authorization check.

findings.claim: The simulated terminal renders the two echo commands as 'Using port 3000 / Starting app'. A real POSIX sh run emits each echo argument followed by a newline, so the slash is output the real script would not show. This is especially misleading in a lesson that asks learners to compare exact observed output with acceptance criteria.

evidence.section: DESCRIPTION and STDOUT: echo writes its arguments to standard output followed by a newline; a newline follows the last argument.

findings.recommendation: Render the simulated script output exactly as two lines ('Using port 3000\nStarting app') in both the first-run and already-checked paths, then keep the failure annotation separate from command stdout. Add a QA assertion for the newline-separated output.

findings.claim: The workspace-scope question labels '~/home/kim' as Kim's home and '~/' as the whole computer. In a POSIX shell, an unquoted '~' expands to $HOME, so '~/home/kim' means a home-relative nested path and '~/' means the home directory, not filesystem root. A second distractor repeats the malformed '~/home/kim/...' path.

evidence.section: 2.6.1 Tilde Expansion: a tilde-prefix consisting only of '~' is replaced by the value of HOME; a following slash remains after that expansion.

findings.recommendation: Use '/home/kim' for the home-folder distractor, an actual file/workspace expression for the too-narrow distractor, and '/' for the whole-computer distractor. Preserve the intended correct answer '/home/kim/work/billing'.
